title: On‑Prem Firewall Telemetry Gaps and Triage Playbook
content:
TL;DR:
We observed a recurring class of customer incidents where control‑plane reachability from our control plane to customer on‑prem gateways failed intermittently. The root cause often traces to customer firewall rules or NAT timeouts, but a consistent problem is poor signal in our telemetry (no denied traffic logs, sparse flow sampling). This doc captures a lightweight triage playbook, quick detection heuristics, and recommended telemetry instrumentation to reduce time‑to‑mitigate.

Context and scope:
- Target: private/VPC and on‑prem deployments where customer perimeter firewalls or reverse proxies sit between Redwood control plane and in‑customer agents.
- Typical failure modes: TCP handshake SYN/ACK asymmetry, long TCP timeouts on keepalives, dropped UDP probes for health checks, intermittent DNAT translation state loss.
- Why this matters: control plane loss leads to job queueing, heartbeat gaps, and failed rollouts; customers see SLA impact even when worker hosts are healthy.

Observed symptoms (field notes):
- Agents report "controlplane_unreachable" with 504s from managed proxies.
- Control-plane side: repeated TCP SYN retransmits to customer gateway, then ICMP unreachable (in some networks).
- Customer side: firewall logs sometimes show ACCEPTs but no application layer sessions; other times logs are missing due to sampling.
- In one incident, NAT translation table exhaustion was correlated with heavy ephemeral port churn from a misconfigured CI job.

Timeline excerpt (representative incident):
- 09:07 UTC: first agent heartbeat gap.
- 09:09 UTC: inbound health check from control plane times out.
- 09:11 UTC: Pager alert (controlplane:reachability P1).
- 09:18 UTC: Oncall runs tcpdump -> sees SYN, no SYN/ACK from customer IP for ~15s window.
- 09:27 UTC: Customer engineering reports firewall was under a high rule refresh causing brief logging outage.

Immediate mitigations (playbook):
1) Detect and confirm
   - Query CONTROLPLANE_METRICS: controlplane_heartbeat_miss{cluster=<id>} >= 3 across 5m.
   - Run quick tcpconnect from control plane egress host: curl --connect-timeout 5 -v telnet://<customer-gateway>:443 (or nc -vz).
   - From a reachable customer-host (if they provide), run curl to our controlplane public IP.
2) Short-term mitigation options to restore connectivity
   - Ask customer to temporarily allow broad management IPs (list attached) / open port for 10 minutes for handshake reestablishment.
   - Switch routing to fallback region if multi‑region control plane is enabled (console -> routing -> force-route).
   - Increase retry/backoff in agent side to smooth ephemeral port churn (config toggle: agent.network.retries=8 -> 16).
3) Evidence collection (do immediately)
   - Capture tcpdump on control plane egress: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <customer-gateway-ip> and save pcap.
   - Ask customer for corresponding firewall logs with timestamps aligned to seconds.
   - Pull netstat/conntrack snapshot from customer host (if allowed): sudo conntrack -L | grep <our-ip>.

Triage checklist (quick steps, ordered):
- Step A: Confirm that control‑plane egress IPs are not in customer blocklist.
- Step B: Validate MTU/path MTU issues: ping -M do -s 1400 <customer> and traceroute -T.
- Step C: Check for NAT translation TTL/timeout mismatch: if customer uses very short UDP/TCP NAT timeouts, consider keepalive tuning.
- Step D: Correlate firewall events to PCAP timestamps (look for SYN/ACK suppressed vs dropped).
- Step E: If flow logs absent, ask for unsampled raw packet capture for 60s window.

Common quick hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Firewall rule refresh cycle causing transient state loss (observed in 38% of reviewed incidents).
- H2: Customer NAT table exhaustion due to ephemeral port churn from parallel jobs.
- H3: Asymmetric routing or active path filter silently dropping return traffic.
- H4: Logging/sampling policy hides denies; firewall actually denied but logs are aggregated/lost.

Telemetry gaps we found (actionable):
- No consistent flow sampling alignment across control plane and customer environment; our flow logs are 1m granularity while customer's sampling is bursty.
- Lack of SYN/SYN-ACK latency histograms on egress hosts.
- No conntrack export from agent footprint; we should export short-lived conntrack counts as metric: agent.conntrack_active{customer_id}.
- Missing source-port entropy metrics; hard to detect port churn patterns.

Proposed instrumentation (short list):
- Add egress TCP SYN latency metric: egress_syn_rtt_ms{region,customer}. Implement using quick TCP handshake probe on a 10s cadence.
- Emit conntrack_count gauge from agent (samples every 15s).
- Tag controlplane_heartbeat_miss with last_successful_egress_ip to speed triage routing.
- Add an event type "telemetry_sampling_gap" when flow logs are delayed >30s.

Runbook patch (commands and canned snippets):
- Capture PCAP on control plane egress: sudo timeout 60 tcpdump -w /tmp/cp-egress-<customer>-$(date +%s).pcap host <gw-ip> and port 443
- Quick conntrack dump (customer side): sudo conntrack -S > /tmp/conntrack-<ts>.log
- Simple curl to emulate agent handshake: curl -v --connect-timeout 6 https://<controlplane-ip>/healthz
- Query metrics (prometheus): curl -s "http://prom:9090/api/v1/query?query=controlplane_heartbeat_miss%7Bcustomer_id%3D%22<id>%22%7D" | jq '.'

Escalation rules and when to involve customer network team:
- If tcpdump shows SYNs with no SYN/ACK for >30s and customer cannot provide matching logs -> engage customer network on call and request live packet capture.
- If conntrack table >90% capacity -> request firewall vendor support and suggest connection rate throttling.
- If flow logs missing during incident -> ask customer to check their log exporter (time drift, log rotation, sampling).

Permanent mitigations and follow-ups (owner assigned):
- Instrumentation owner: Priya Nair -> implement egress_syn_rtt_ms and conntrack_count by EOW (2026-03-19).
- Customer playbook template: Diego Alvarez -> create a one‑pager for customer network teams describing recommended firewall states and expected logs.
- Console feature: product -> add a per‑customer controlplane reachability timeline widget (linked to pcaps/notes).

Open action items (short):
- [ ] Add agent metric for conntrack_count (Priya)
- [ ] Create SLA checklist template for onboarding customers with stateful firewalls (Diego)
- [ ] Update runbook to include known vendor caveats (Fortinet/Sophos/AZFW) (Maya)
- [ ] Create alert annotation that links to last 3 pcaps when controlplane_heartbeat_miss triggers.

Notes to self (oncall tips):
- Always collect pcaps even if you think it’s a logging gap; logs are often rotated / sampled.
- When asking customers to open ports, give them exact CIDR blocks and a 10–15 minute window; many ops teams prefer limited-duration temporary exceptions.
- For intermittent problems, ask for a conntrack snapshot before and after a short synthetic test.

Appendix: quick vendor notes
- Fortinet: default conntrack timeout for TCP can be >300s but admin tools may trigger aggressive pruning during configuration pushes.
- Palo Alto: flow logs sometimes go to a separate collector; check collector health when logs are missing.
- Azure Firewall: logging is routed via diagnostic settings; missing logs often caused by retention policy misconfiguration.

Contact / ownership
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (SRE)
- Instrumentation owner: Priya Nair
- Customer playbook owner: Diego Alvarez

If you make runbook edits, prefix the filename with the date and your initials. Keep this doc as a working draft until the telemetry additions are live.

End of doc.
